# sf2-themes

> Street Fighter II color themes for WezTerm, Herdr, Neovim, Codex, Starship, Lazygit, and Claude Code.

sf2-themes is a single-binary CLI named `sf2-themes`, also linked as `sf2`, for macOS and Linux on arm64 and amd64. It has no runtime dependencies. It installs a 36-theme TOML catalog (dark and light main variants plus the Super Street Fighter II Turbo roster) into WezTerm, Herdr, Neovim, Codex, Starship, Lazygit, and Claude Code.

Live site: https://douglasjarquin.github.io/sf2-themes/
Repository: https://github.com/douglasjarquin/sf2-themes

Install the latest release into ~/.local/bin:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://github.com/douglasjarquin/sf2-themes/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh
```

Pin a release by piping into `SF2_THEMES_VERSION=2.0.0 sh` instead. If a 1.x copy installed with uv is present, run `uv tool uninstall sf2-themes` first.

Catalog ids stay short (`ryu`, `ken-light`). Installed identities use `sf2-<catalog-id>`.

Then apply a theme to an app. `sf2 apps` lists the app ids, and `--dry-run` prints every write without making it:

```sh
sf2 apps
sf2 apply wezterm --theme ryu
sf2 apply nvim --theme ken-light --dry-run
```

- [Install](https://github.com/douglasjarquin/sf2-themes/blob/main/docs/sf2-themes/install.md): the installer, version pins, verification, and upgrading from 1.x
- [Apply and setup](https://github.com/douglasjarquin/sf2-themes/blob/main/docs/sf2-themes/setup-and-apply.md): apply a theme to each app in one step, ownership rules, --adopt, and --dry-run
- [Commands](https://github.com/douglasjarquin/sf2-themes/blob/main/docs/sf2-themes/commands.md): apps, themes, show, validate, current, and boss aliases
- [File writes](https://github.com/douglasjarquin/sf2-themes/blob/main/docs/sf2-themes/file-writes.md): paths, overrides, symlinks, and backups
- [Uninstall](https://github.com/douglasjarquin/sf2-themes/blob/main/docs/sf2-themes/uninstall.md): files and settings to remove
- [Changelog](https://github.com/douglasjarquin/sf2-themes/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): what changed in each release
